Priya (Support): FYI ACME (acct: acme-corp) opened a critical ticket #12345 — they say objects that hit TTL 30d are still visible after 45d. Customer insists we didn't delete per their retention settings. They included a few object ids. Can someone triage? :eyes:

Ethan (SRE): Can you paste one object id + the API call they used? quick check: was response 202 or an error?

Priya (Support): obj-abc123, obj-def456. They called our delete endpoint via our SDK and also tried management UI purge. From their logs: `202 Accepted` followed by still-returning 200 on GET. Sample curl they ran: 
```
curl -X DELETE "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj-abc123" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```
They also included an internal webhook payload showing `status: active` after 45 days.

RetentionBot: Automated notice — retention policy for acme-corp updated to `custom: 365d` by `legal@acme.com` at 1765000010.

Alex D: Hmm, two possibilities: 1) custom retention was applied at org/bucket level so TTL from object metadata ignored, or 2) deletion jobs failed (KMS decrypt or HSM hold). Can you confirm which retention layer applies to those objects?

Jules (SecOps): I queried KMS for key `kms-acme-01`: there is an active legal hold flag `HOLD: true` and a recent operation `HOLD_APPLIED` by `legal@acme.com` at 1764999999. If legal hold exists we intentionally prevent deletes. Also seeing `hsm_lock: engaged` on the key.

Ethan (SRE): I pulled the delete worker logs for the timeframe the objects should have been purged. Relevant snippet: 
```
[2026-02-10 12:34:56] delete_worker obj-abc123 starting purge
[2026-02-10 12:34:56] delete_worker obj-abc123 error: DecryptError: KMS access denied (key kms-acme-01)
[2026-02-10 12:34:56] delete_worker obj-abc123 mark: pending_retry
```
So the pipeline attempted deletion but KMS denied decrypt, which leaves object visible. That aligns with Jules' hold.

Priya (Support): Customer says they never asked for a legal hold. They want a timeline and to remove the hold if it's internal. How do we prove who applied it?

Jules (SecOps): Audit log entry exists: `action: HOLD_APPLY, actor: legal@acme.com, src: console, ts: 1764999999`. If customer IAM user initiated it we can point them to their admin console. If it shows our support/service account, escalate. For immediate remediation: legal hold must be removed by the actor or an authorized admin. I cannot remove it unilaterally.

Ethan (SRE): Short repro you can give customer to show object is retained by policy: GET metadata returns `"retention_state": "locked", "retention_policy": "org:custom:365d", "kms_key": "kms-acme-01"`. Example response: 
```
GET /v1/objects/obj-abc123
{
  "id": "obj-abc123",
  "status": "active",
  "retention_state": "locked",
  "ttl_expires_at": "2026-01-02T12:00:00Z"
}
```
That demonstrates policy override.

Priya (Support): Ok I'll ask the customer to confirm whether `legal@acme.com` corresponds to them. If they confirm it's internal, they can remove hold from console or request us to validate owner. Meanwhile I'll set expectations: we cannot force-delete while hold exists.

Alex D: Also note edge-case where key rotation/in-progress HSM ops can temporarily block decrypts; if customer confirms no hold we should check key rotation job history (Jules).

Jules (SecOps): Verified: `rotation_job` completed earlier; the hold event is the blocker, not rotation. Audit export attached to ticket.

Priya (Support): Thanks all. Next actions: 1) I'll ping ACME legal contact to validate `legal@acme.com`. 2) If they confirm hold was in error, they'll remove it and we'll re-run deletion jobs (Ethan, can you queue a priority purge once cleared?). 3) I'll attach audit log slice to ticket and mark high.

Ethan (SRE): Yep I can queue a manual purge run for those object ids once hold lifted. Add me to the ticket and I’ll run a one-off: `DELETE /internal/admin/purge?ids=obj-abc123,obj-def456` (requires SecOps OK). :thumbsup:

Priya (Support): Adding notes to #12345 and cc'ing ACME-CS. Closing loop here until customer responds. :locked:
